text: The pivotal sentence in Genesis 6 concerns God’s inner life. Yahweh sees that “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” and Yahweh is sorry that he made man: “it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart” (Genesis 6:5–6). That grief comes before the sentence of judgment and gives the judgment its character, since the flood is moved by a maker’s sorrow over what his creatures have become. Before any rain falls, the first covenant in Scripture appears: “But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons’ wives with thee” (Genesis 6:18). The promise reaches beyond Noah to the animals, “two of every sort,” and to the food that will keep them all alive (Genesis 6:19–21). Genesis 6 announces “the end of all flesh” and also arranges, in detail, what will survive it: the one man who found favor is told to gather in the creatures God is about to drown.
